_notes: A friar's summers (E3): the order's, not the diocesan seminary's. `houses` names the kind of house the formation year is lived in that the summer fits: a novice's summer stays in the novitiate; a student's goes where the province sends students. `orders` narrows to one order where the summer is its own. Effects use the pillars and the religious constituencies. Institutions are generated analogs, never named.

summers.label: The novitiate's summer
summers.blurb: The canonical year does not stop for July. The garden, the kitchen, the Office at its hours, the novice master's conferences moved to the porch, and the silence, which is harder in the heat.
summers.outcome: You weed, and cook badly, and say the Office at its hours with the windows open, and by August the silence has stopped being a rule and started being a place you go. The novice master's report says you kept the summer, which is what it is meant to say.

summers.label: The walking pilgrimage
summers.blurb: Three weeks on foot with the novice master and the other novices, shrine to shrine, sleeping in parish halls, begging supper at rectories that have been expecting you since the founder's day.
summers.outcome: Three weeks of road, blisters, the Office said walking, and a rectory in a small town where the pastor fed nine novices and wept at the door. You come back thinner and closer to the men you walked with than to anyone you have known.

summers.label: The province's mission
summers.blurb: Ten weeks at the mission the province has kept for a century, a country away: a friar who has been there thirty years, a language you half have, catechists who know more than you.
summers.outcome: You come back with a tan, a parasite, forty words of a language nobody at the studium speaks, and a letter from the old missionary to the provincial that you are not shown and that is read at your profession.

summers.label: A Dominican parish
summers.blurb: A summer in a parish entrusted to the order, under a friar pastor who preaches like the founder and administers like nobody: the youth group, the funerals, the sacristy at six.
summers.outcome: You learn what a parish is from a man who has run one for twenty years in a habit, and what it costs him, and come back with the youth group's t-shirt and an opinion about pastors.

summers.label: The studium's summer languages
summers.blurb: Eight weeks of Latin and Greek at the studium with the lector who does not believe in summers, four hours a morning, and the afternoons in the library because there is nowhere else to be.
summers.outcome: By August you can read Thomas in Latin without a dictionary on the desk, which changes theology from a subject into a language, and the lector says, once, that you might be sent on, which is the most he says.

summers.label: The summer preaching
summers.blurb: The province sends its students out in pairs to the youth camps and the parish missions, to preach four talks a week to teenagers who did not ask for them and to parishes that did.
summers.outcome: Forty talks in ten weeks to people who could get up and leave, some of whom did. By the end you can hold a hall. The friar you were paired with says you will be a preacher, in the tone the order uses for that.

summers.label: Helping at the novitiate
summers.blurb: A summer back at the novitiate as the novice master's second pair of hands: the garden, the horarium, and eight novices who look at you as if you knew something.
summers.outcome: You keep a house's summer with a man who has kept thirty of them, and learn what he was doing when you thought he was doing nothing. The novices remember you. The novice master remembers you differently.

summers.label: The province's school
summers.blurb: Summer school at the high school the province has run since the immigrants built it: forty boys who failed something, a classroom with one fan, and a headmaster in a habit who has seen everything.
summers.outcome: You teach algebra to boys who did not want it, and coach a team you did not know the rules of, and by August two of them are asking about the Order and one of them means it. The headmaster writes the provincial a line.

summers.label: The province's mission
summers.blurb: Ten weeks at the mission a country away, where the province has three friars and eleven parishes and a truck: catechists, baptisms by the hundred, and a language you half have.
summers.outcome: You come back with a tan, a parasite, forty words of a language nobody at the studium speaks, and a letter from the mission's superior to the provincial that is read at your profession.

summers.label: An Augustinian parish
summers.blurb: A summer in a parish the order has kept for a hundred years, under a friar pastor who has been there for twenty: the funerals, the festival, the friary kitchen at eleven at night.
summers.outcome: You learn what a parish is from a man who runs one in a habit, and what the friary is for at the end of a day like that, and come back with an opinion about pastors and a place at that table for life.

summers.label: The shrine
summers.blurb: A summer at the province's shrine, where the buses come: confessions eight hours a day for the older friars to hear and the students to schedule, the candles, the gift shop, and a novena every week.
summers.outcome: You see more of the Church's people in ten weeks than a parish sees in a year, and learn what they come to a shrine for, which is not what the guidebook says. The rector of the shrine tells the provincial you have a gift for the door.

summers.label: The summer with Augustine
summers.blurb: Eight weeks in the studium's library with the old professor who has read all of Augustine and means to see you read a fair part of him, in Latin, one dialogue a week.
summers.outcome: By August you have the father's voice in your head in his own language, which changes the Rule from a text into a man, and the professor says, once, that you might be sent on.

summers.label: Hospital chaplaincy
summers.blurb: A summer of clinical pastoral education at the city hospital: the dying, the families, and a supervisor who will ask you how you feel about it every Wednesday until you tell her.
summers.outcome: You learn to walk into a room where someone is dying and stay, which is most of the priesthood, and to say what you felt about it aloud, which is most of the rest. The habit turns out to open doors in a hospital that a collar does not.

summers.label: Spanish immersion
summers.blurb: Ten weeks with the order's house in a country where the language is spoken: classes in the morning, a barrio parish in the afternoon, and the Office in a language that makes the psalms new.
summers.outcome: You come back able to hear a confession in Spanish and preach a homily in it that a patient parish can follow, which the province, with the parishes it has, notices at once.
